correctness.rationale: The proof partitions all unordered pairs into surviving cross-part pairs, deleted matched pairs, same-side pairs in the first part, and same-side pairs in the second part. For a deleted pair, every geodesic has length three and the only forbidden middle choices are the other deleted matched pairs, giving \((a-1)(b-1)-t+1\). Same-side counts follow from common-neighbor loss. Summation yields the formula, and the optimization is the exact maximum of the concave quadratic \(t(C-t)\). The standalone breadth-first-search checker independently confirms 199 parameter cases for \(3\le a,b\le8\).

value.rationale: The family is singled out explicitly by the initiating paper as a plausible improvement over balanced complete bipartite graphs. The theorem turns that suggestion into an exact formula, determines the best matching-deletion size for every \(a,b\ge3\), and gives an infinite family of bipartite graphs that strictly improve on \(K_{n,n}\) for \(n\ge5\). This is a natural structural step toward the stated bipartite extremal problem rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
